Have you been suffering from chronic gastrointestinal symptoms like abdominal pain or heartburn for many years? Additionally, do you have a family history of this type of blood disorder?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 8.3 g/dL (low); WBC: 81,000 /mm3 (elevated); Platelets: 35,600 /mm3 (low); Peripheral Blood Smear: Presence of immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL).

The combination of severe pancytopenia (low hemoglobin and platelets) with an alarming leukocytosis (81,000) and the pathognomonic finding of Auer rods (pink, needle-shaped inclusions) on the smear is diagnostic for this medical emergency. This requires immediate initiation of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) to prevent fatal disseminated intravascular coagulation.
